To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the time behaviour K-electron capture decays of 180mRe and 142mPm in solid state targets is not consistent with the explanation of "GSI Oscillation" by means of the interference between the two closely spaced ground states.
the experimental data on EC decays of atoms in solid targets do not support the existence of two close ground mass-eigenstate in 180Re and in 142Pm.

the time behaviour of K-shell EC decays of atoms in solid targets is not sensitive to the presence of two closely spaced mass eigenstates of the mother nucleus and, therefore, cannot be used to prove or refute the hypothesis of the existence of such states.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) What is the nature of the observed time behaviour of EC-decay rates?
the analysis of the experimental results obtained at GSI on the time behaviour of the K-shell electron capture decays of 180mRe (T1/2 = 1.5 h) and 142Pmb (T1/ 2 = 1 min).

the following questions: (a) What is the reason for the absence of time modulation of the K-shell EC decay of the atoms 180Re, 142Pm? (b) What is the explanation of the GSI oscillations? (c) Is there a connection of the K-shell capture of the electrons from the inner shells of the atoms with the nuclear shell structure of the daughter nucleus
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no experimental evidence of the existence of two ground states of the 180Re and the 142Pm nuclei.
the "GSI oscillations" do not exist.
the GSI Oscillations are not observed in 180Re and are not observed in a solid target in 142Pm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the "GSI oscillations" are an artifact of the experiment.
the "GSI oscillations" are not a signature of two mass eigenstates of the mother nucleus, but a signature of a single mass eigenstate.
the GSI Oscillation data can be described by the two-state model, if one of the two mass eigenstates has a very small width.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the observed time behaviour of K-shell EC decays of the mother nuclei 180Re and142Pm can be described by the standard theory, without invoking the existence of two closely spaced mass eigenstates.
the observed time dependence of the EC decay rate of atoms 180mRe and 142mPm is not caused by the interference between the ground mass-eigenstate and the first excited mass-eigenstate.
the K-shell EC decay is a single-state process.
